messages:
zoe: Heads-up — after we applied the RBAC tidy for keystore-access plus the TLS cipher hardening in apac-canary, several services reported mTLS failures. Proxy logs show KMS unwrap/sign DENY. Please triage. :eyes:

marco: Example from api-egress-apac-3:
```
2026-03-25T21:08:12Z api-egress-apac-3 audit=crypto DENY unwrap key=projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/egress/cryptoKeys/egress-keystore labels=[region:apac] principal=svc-account:payments-apac@dataplane reason=permissionDenied
```
TLS alert: KEY_UNWRAP_FAILURE

anil: I saw the same pattern. RBAC change removed kms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt for cross-region proxies when we dedupbed 'inactive' principals. The pruning rule was too aggressive and matched service accounts that rotate rarely.

infra-bot: policy-change "keystore-prune-apac-2026-03-25" applied by @zoe at 2026-03-25T21:05:43Z. Recommended rollback if production crypto ops fail.

zoe: Rolling back now. While rollback happens, can we enable proxy cached-key fallback for 120s to reduce impact? Command: `kubectl -n proxy annotate deploy/egress-proxy keystore.cache-ttl=120`

marco: Rollback applied at 21:11 UTC. KMS audit shows unwraps succeeding for previously denied principals; proxies recovered within ~90s.

anil: Postmortem items: 1) Add log-based alert for KMS DENY unwrap/asymmetricSign spikes (>4/min) 2) Add preflight in policy CI to run `gcloud kms keys test-iam-permissions` for decrypt/sign on all principals targeted by a prune 3) Disallow overlapping crypto RBAC changes and TLS hardening in the same deploy window (add gating rule).

sec-oncall: Incident created INC-6022. Schedule 30m RCA. Please attach policy-diff, KMS audit export and deploy calendar entries.

zoe: Thanks. Also proposal: enrich key labels with region aliases and include a step in policy MR template to enumerate 'recent principals' by querying KMS audit to avoid removing active accounts. I'll open an MR.
